title: Micro-Mobility Services
desc: Plan and run a small shared bike or scooter service: fleet, safety, parking, pricing, maintenance and city rules.
outcomes: Explain micro-mobility types and where they fit.
Plan fleet size, zones and parking.
task: Plan a 30-day pilot of a shared micro-mobility service for one campus or district, with fleet, safety rules, maintenance, pricing and a community plan.
condition: A computer, a map, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. Real vehicles are not required.
standard: Fleet and cost maths correct; safety rules and rider age limits stated; parking and permits checked; maintenance plan has daily checks; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Campus managers, tourism staff, city assistants, entrepreneurs.
evidence: zone map, fleet sheet, safety rules, price sheet, maintenance plan
modules: Types, fit and local conditions
Understand
Different vehicles suit different places. Match the vehicle to the streets, the weather and the riders.
Bikes, e-bikes, scooters, cargo bikes and adaptive trikes have different range, speed, cost and injury risk.
Short trips under 5 km are the main use; e-assist helps on hills and with longer trips.
Check street width, slopes, surface, rain and heat before choosing.
Scooters have higher injury risk at speed; plan speed limits.
A flat tourist promenade suits light bikes. A hilly university suits e-bikes with 60 km range. A district with wide pavements may allow scooters with a 15 km/h limit.
Compare three vehicle types for one site in a table.
Table has range, cost, risk and fit.
Zones, parking and rules
Apply
Order on the street keeps the service welcome.
Place parking where people already walk: gates, stations and shops.
Use geofencing in the app to slow vehicles in busy zones or end trips only in marked bays.
Mark no-go zones near hospitals and schools.
Work with the owner or authority.
A campus limits scooters to 10 km/h in the library courtyard through the app and marks bays at four gates.
Draw a zone map for a campus or district.
Zones are marked and justified.
Fleet sizing and rebalancing
Analyse
Not too many and not too few vehicles.
Fleet = peak trips / trips per vehicle per day.
Keep 15 to 20 per cent of vehicles under repair or charging.
Use trip data to move vehicles before peak times.
Start small and measure.
60 peak trips at 6 trips per vehicle need 10 vehicles plus 2 spares. With 20 per cent unavailable, only about 10 are on the street at once.
Size a fleet for your case with spare allowance.
Maths correct.
Rider safety
Evaluate
Prevent injuries.
Helmets, lights, speed limits and age limits.
A short in-app safety quiz before the first ride.
Incident log, insurance and clear parking rules.
Share lessons weekly.
After a five-question quiz is added, near misses fall by a third in a month. A slow zone near pedestrians reduces collisions.
Write safety rules and a first-ride quiz of five questions.
Rules are measurable and the quiz is clear.
Maintenance and charging
Apply
Safe vehicles every day.
Daily check: brakes, tyres, lights, bell and lock.
Replace worn tyres and pads on a schedule.
Train staff to handle batteries; never charge damaged packs.
Keep spare parts and a repair log.
A weekly brake and tyre check finds three worn pads before any incident. A tag shows the last check date.
Create a check card and weekly calendar.
Card has ten items and calendar is complete.
Pricing, access and money
Evaluate
Cover costs and stay fair.
Unlock fee plus per-minute price; day and weekly passes.
Costs: vehicles, staff, charging, repair, insurance and permits.
Student and low-income discounts.
Break-even trips per vehicle per day.
Revenue of 90 INR per vehicle-day against a cost of 70 INR gives a 20 INR margin. Break-even is 3.5 trips at a 20 INR average fare.
Build a pricing sheet and test two prices.
Currency shown and totals correct.
Community and environment
Evaluate
Be a good neighbour.
Noise, clutter and accessibility.
Complaint line with a 24-hour response.
Recycling of batteries and parts.
Adaptations for riders with disabilities where possible.
A trike option and a pickup service help riders who cannot use a scooter. A fine for blocking paths is explained and enforced fairly.
List community actions and owners.
Each has an owner and a date.
Pilot plan and stop rules
Create
Test before scaling.
Targets for trips, safety and complaints.
Stop rules: pause if serious injuries occur.
Review weekly and report monthly.
Decide: stop, change or grow.
The pilot is paused after two incidents to review rules, then resumed with stricter zones and a rider quiz.
Present the plan with stop rules.
Targets are numbers and stop rules are stated.
quiz: Typical trip length?
Under about 5 km. (Covered in module 1: Types, fit and local conditions. To pass that module: Table has range, cost, risk and fit.)
Fleet formula?
Peak trips / trips per vehicle per day. (Covered in module 3: Fleet sizing and rebalancing. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Name a safety rule.
Helmets or speed limits. (Covered in module 4: Rider safety. To pass that module: Rules are measurable and the quiz is clear.)
Daily check items?
Brakes, tyres, lights, bell, lock. (Covered in module 5: Maintenance and charging. To pass that module: Card has ten items and calendar is complete.)
Break-even idea?
Trips per day needed to cover costs. (Covered in module 6: Pricing, access and money. To pass that module: Currency shown and totals correct.)
Why parking zones?
To avoid clutter. (Covered in module 2: Zones, parking and rules. To pass that module: Zones are marked and justified.)
Why insurance?
Covers incidents. (Covered in module 4: Rider safety. To pass that module: Rules are measurable and the quiz is clear.)
What is rebalancing?
Moving vehicles to demand. (Covered in module 3: Fleet sizing and rebalancing. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Name a community issue.
Noise or blocked paths. (Covered in module 7: Community and environment. To pass that module: Each has an owner and a date.)
What is a pilot?
A short test before scaling. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan and stop rules. To pass that module: Targets are numbers and stop rules are stated.)
